currentContext.expansion: The annual report contains no named expansion project, commissioning timeline or capacity-addition programme. The only forward capacity language is the Chairman's stated strategic vision: 'We aim to expand our manufacturing capacity, invest in advanced technologies, and strengthen our presence in both domestic and international markets' — with no project, site, size, cost or date attached. On the existing base, the MD&A states only that the Company is 'presently equipped with such a manufacturing facility capable of producing CPP & CPE films spanning a thickness range from 15 to 250 microns' (a product specification, not an installed capacity). Management describes the year's operating response as cost optimisation, improving operational efficiencies and 'enhancing capacity utilization' rather than adding capacity, and the technology-absorption disclosure notes only process development work to improve production efficiency and yield on existing products. The Board explicitly states that no capital investment was made on energy-conservation equipment during the financial year, that R&D expenditure was 'None', and that no technology was imported. Post year-end corporate actions (an increase in authorised share capital and the addition of agro/agri/food products to the Main Objects, both approved at the EGM of 27 June 2026) may enable future investment, but no capex plan is disclosed against them.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and crude-oil linkage
risks.note: Management attributes the year's decline in revenue and profitability to 'fluctuations in raw material prices' and cites 'elevated raw material prices, volatility in crude oil prices' as a pressure on the packaging industry — polymer input cost is the dominant swing factor for a CPP/CPE film maker with limited pass-through in a weak-demand year

FY2025-26 is described as 'a challenging operating environment, with pressure on demand ... and global economic uncertainties', with 'subdued demand across certain end-user segments'; revenue from operations fell to Rs 6,001.30 lakhs from Rs 8,530.75 lakhs and the Company witnessed a decline in both revenue and profitability

MD&A Risks & Concerns: 'the chance that competitive forces could prevent the Company from achieving its goal on account of declining revenues or margins' — a commodity-adjacent film business with no disclosed capacity or cost advantage

MD&A names 'logistical, economic, political, cultural, competitive and infrastructural concerns'; mitigation is supplier diversification and a management strategy against disruptions. Higher logistics costs are separately cited by the Chairman as a pressure during the year

A material share of activity is cross-border — foreign exchange earned of Rs 2,113.33 lakh against foreign exchange outgo of Rs 1,584.00 lakh during FY26 — leaving earnings exposed to currency movement and to trade/tariff conditions in export markets; the MD&A itself frames opportunity around US, UAE and UK plastics trade
MD&A flags 'critical skill shortages, increasing staff attrition or significant workforce retirement'; mitigation is training, HR practices and rewards to retain talent

MD&A flags sovereign policy changes that 'adversely impact the financial stability of the Company' and compliance risk carrying 'legal and financial penalties for failing to act under internal and external regulations'; plastics packaging is a directly regulated end-use

risks.risk: Dependence on related-party premises and concentrated family control
risks.note: Key operating premises sit inside related-party arrangements — a five-year rent agreement with associate 3B Flexipacks Private Limited over the Masar, Padra premises running only to 18.05.2027, and a Hans Export lease whose stated term ended 31.07.2025 — alongside unsecured loans from Babariya-family KMPs, so continuity of premises and funding rests on associate/family entities. A Non-Executive Independent Director (Ms. Mital Devani) also resigned with effect from 30 May 2026

risks.risk: Execution risk on the newly added agro/food vertical
risks.note: Members approved by Special Resolution on 27 June 2026 the insertion of agro/agri/food products (spices, oilseeds, grains, vegetables, herbs, pickles) into the Main Objects — an unrelated diversification for a CPP/CPE film manufacturer, disclosed with no plan, investment or timeline, alongside an approved increase in authorised share capital
